pairs.reason: Both would redraw the limits on the courts, possibly with a Knesset override, but one has the elected majority do it and the other requires a broad compromise not set by one side.
One gives elected officials more power over judges and the attorney general; the other reverses those changes and protects their independence in a basic law.
Both keep the changes already passed, including the law on choosing judges, but one continues with further changes and the other stops there; the directions differ and the lower is used.
Both fix the rules in a constitution or basic law, but one leaves the content to a broad compromise, possibly with an override, and the other reverses the changes and protects the courts.
Both avoid one side pushing its changes further, but one writes a new constitutional framework and the other wants no further change beyond small adjustments.
Both stop further changes that weaken the courts, but one reverses what was passed and adds protection in a basic law while the other rules out any reversal.
